sources.text:
10 wk summer placement, Brightwater Analytics (small fintech), Manchester, Jun-Aug 2026
team: me + 2 platform engineers (Mateo, Jen)
- goal: move the nightly risk batch jobs off one big VM onto EKS so they stop blocking each other
- stack: Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus, Loki
- decision: spot instances for the batch node pool, on-demand for the Argo controller. cheaper, jobs are retryable anyway
- problem: jobs randomly lost progress overnight, ~5% of runs. cause: spot interruptions + checkpoints only every 10 min
- investigated via node termination events in CloudWatch + the job logs. the 2 min warning wasn't enough
- fix: checkpoint every 90 s + a drain handler on the termination notice
- result: nightly run 4h10m -> 2h35m, nothing blocked since
- learned: read the spot termination docs first, not after
- why Graphcore: liked the scheduling side more than the models. want to work on the platform under the models
I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools and the Karpenter autoscaler config myself, and Mateo reviewed them.

documents.text:
During a ten-week summer placement at Brightwater Analytics in Manchester, our three-person platform team moved the nightly risk batch jobs from a single virtual machine onto EKS. The team was me plus two platform engineers, Mateo and Jen.

The stack included Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus and Loki. The decision was to use spot instances for the batch node pool and on-demand for the Argo controller. The jobs are retryable so that spot choice was cheaper.

Jobs randomly lost progress overnight in about 5% of runs. The cause was spot interruptions plus checkpoints only every 10 min. Investigation was via node termination events in CloudWatch and the job logs. It found the 2 min warning was not enough. The fix was a checkpoint every 90 s and a drain handler on the termination notice. The lesson was to read the spot termination docs first, not after.

I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools and reviewed Mateo's Karpenter autoscaler config. Mateo reviewed the Terraform modules and Karpenter autoscaler config.

Dear Graphcore hiring team,

I am applying for the Graduate Cloud Platform Engineer 2027 role at Graphcore.

I want to join Graphcore because I liked the scheduling side more than the models and want to work on the platform under the models.

I completed a 10 week summer placement at Brightwater Analytics in Manchester from June to August 2026. We worked as a team of me plus two platform engineers, Mateo and Jen. Our goal was to move the nightly risk batch jobs off one big VM onto EKS to stop blocking. The stack included Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus and Loki. We decided on spot instances for the batch node pool and on-demand for the Argo controller. The jobs were retryable so the spot choice was cheaper. I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools and the Karpenter autoscaler config myself, and Mateo reviewed them.

We saw that jobs lost progress overnight in around 5 percent of runs. We investigated this via node termination events in CloudWatch and the job logs. The cause was spot interruptions plus checkpoints only every 10 minutes. We found the 2 minute warning was not enough. We fixed this with a checkpoint every 90 seconds and a drain handler on the termination notice. I learned to read the spot termination docs first not after.

Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards,
